title: Reading notes - LLM inference optimizations (quantization, KV cache, batching)
content:
Objective: jot down quick takeaways from recent papers/blogs + ideas for small experiments we can run on Dedicated/private to validate cost/latency tradeoffs. Mostly a scratchpad - TODOs and hypotheses included.

Papers/links skimmed (quick notes):
- "Memory-Efficient Attention" (arXiv 2024) - main idea: reduce KV memory by chunked attention + recompute. + Good for very long contexts; trade: CPU recompute overhead.
  - Implication for Redwood: could help on long-chat sessions for LLMs where KV size dominates GPU memory. Potential microbenchmark: 8k/32k context for 7B/13B model, measure throughput vs peak memory.
- "Quantization-aware Inference" (blog: bitsandbytes/2024 post) - 4-bit/3-bit mixed precision with better calibration + per-channel scaling.
  - Notes: quality drop varies by model family; OTP: run eval set (prod prompt suite, small) to measure generation quality degradation per quant level.
- "Sparse & Mixture-of-Experts inference optimizations" (conference talk) - routing overhead can blow latency; only helpful if sparsity reduces compute enough to offset routing.

Key takeaways and short hypotheses: 
- KV cache trimming: For short-turn conversations, prefix caching gives big wins. Hypothesis: an LRU-style per-user prefix cache + lightweight signature will reduce token cost by ~4-10% on chat workloads. Experiment: enable prefix cache on Dedicated pool (small) and measure token count and latency 24h. Link to eval ticket: JIRA-MLINF-1024.
- Quantization: default to q4f16 for 13B models for a baseline; run q3/q4/q5 to see cost vs PPL/ROUGE on our eval prompts. Hypothesis: q4 yields ~30% cost reduction with <2% quality drop on most prompts.
- Batching policy tuning: continuous batching with dynamic watermarks looks promising; but tail latency sometimes spikes. Idea: implement adaptive max_batch_size per model variant based on recent p95 latency. Small rollout: add feature-flagged policy handler in serving-runtime to test.

Notes on experiments (quick plan):
- Bench1: Memory vs throughput (KV strategies)
  - Models: redwood-13b, redwood-7b-ctx32k
  - Metrics: throughput (tokens/s), p50/p95 latency, GPU memory utilization, cost-per-token estimate.
  - Baseline: current runtime w/ prefix-only caching
  - Variants: chunked-attention recompute; aggressive KV eviction after N turns; per-user prefix cache with TTL
- Bench2: Quantization quality sweep
  - Models: 7B, 13B; quant levels: fp16, q4f16, q3, q5
  - Eval: subset of prod prompts (100 prompts), automated scoring (BLEU/ROUGE where applicable) + human spot-check (5 prompts)

Potential risks / unknowns:
- Recompute strategies may increase GPU utilization and degrade latency SLOs for real-time apps. Need to measure p95 carefully.
- Quantization often interacts with tokenization quirks; watch for generation degeneration (repetition).

Action items (short):
- [ ] Create JIRA spike for KV memory microbench (assign to Ryan) - JIRA-MLINF-1024
- [ ] Spin up Dedicated small pool (2xA10x1) for experiments (request via infra: infra-request-2025-02)
- [ ] Write evaluation harness to run quant sweep (use existing eval infra, reuse EvalSuite from repo) - I can draft a PR: github link above.
- [ ] Sync with SRE on acceptable p95 thresholds for experimental clusters (Evelyn/Ping)

Brainstorm / longer-term ideas (bullets):
- Model-aware kernel selection: runtime picks kernels not just by model arch but by prompt length distribution (hot path optimization).
- Lightweight signature for user sessions to allow cross-request prefix reuse across restarts (requires security review).
- Offer "latency-first" vs "cost-first" serving mode in Console: different batching/cache/quant configs exposed.

Random notes to self:
- Check notes from ICLR talk (Hannah Lee) about reranking on-device - could reduce generation tokens for top-k rerank.
- Follow up with Research: ask about recent evals on q3 quantization behavior across instruction-tuned models.

References to save:
- arXiv: https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.14130
- bitsandbytes blog: https://github.com/facebookresearch/bitsandbytes
- internal PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/482

Misc (scratch):
- Slack thread: #eng-serving-runtime "kv-cache idea" (link above)
- Confluence draft: /spaces/ML/pages/kv-cache-design (CONFLUENCE-ML/kv-cache-design)

End of notes.
\-- I.M.
